title: Apostle to the apostles (John 20:11–18)
hook: Mary Magdalene is sent to tell the others; Pope Francis raised her day to a feast in 2016

segments.voice: Yesterday, blood and water from the opened side. Your line was they shall look on him. Where did you stop and really look at a cross? Day five hundred thirty-one.

Early Sunday morning, still dark. Mary Magdalene has come to the tomb and found the stone rolled away. She ran for Peter and the beloved disciple. They came running, saw the linen cloths lying there, and went home. She didn't. She's standing outside the tomb, crying. Anyone who has lost someone knows that kind of crying: the kind where you can't leave, because leaving would make it real. Everyone else has gone. And she's the one who stays.
screen: `THE STONE ROLLED AWAY.` → `THE MEN GO HOME.` → `SHE STAYS, CRYING.`

segments.voice: She stoops to look into the tomb and sees two angels where the body had been. Woman, why weepest thou? Because they have taken away my Lord, she says, and I know not where they have laid him. She turns and sees a man she takes for the gardener. Sir, if you've carried him off, tell me where, and I'll take him away. Then he says one word. In the Douay-Rheims: "Jesus saith to her: Mary. She turning, saith to him: Rabboni (which is to say, Master)." Not a speech. Her name. The good shepherd said his sheep know his voice when he calls them by name, and here it happens. Then Jesus says, do not touch me, for I am not yet ascended. The Latin, noli me tangere, gave its name to hundreds of paintings. The Greek may mean something closer to, don't hold on to me, don't cling. Because she has a job. Go to my brethren, he says, and tell them. And she does. The text says: Mary Magdalen cometh and telleth the disciples, "I have seen the Lord," and what he said to her. She's the first person in John's Gospel sent to announce the resurrection, sent to the apostles themselves. Very early, Christian writers gave her a title for it: apostle to the apostles. Apostle means one who is sent. In 2016 Pope Francis raised her day, July 22, from a memorial to a feast, the same rank as the feasts of the apostles, and the decree used that old title.
screen: `WOMAN, WHY WEEPEST THOU?` · `ONE WORD: MARY.` · `DON'T CLING; GO AND TELL.` · `JULY 22, A FEAST SINCE 2016.` · then, large: `APOSTLE TO THE APOSTLES.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: get ready to tell someone good news. Sit, and breathe. Think back over the last week or so for something genuinely good: a recovery, a kindness you saw, a small win, a reconciliation, a baby, a sunrise. Let it fill your chest for a moment. Then think of who would be glad to hear it. Picture their face when you tell them. If you pray, you can hold Mary's words, I have seen the Lord, and give thanks. If you don't, just enjoy the good news before you pass it on. The bell holds the time.
Apostle to the apostles. The old title for Mary Magdalene, the first sent to tell the disciples that Jesus is risen. Today's word.
Your line: I have seen the lord. Today, tell that good news to the person you pictured, in person if you can. Day five hundred thirty-one.

screen: `DAY 531 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: RECEIVE YE THE HOLY GHOST.`

howItsDone: Catholics celebrate the Feast of Saint Mary Magdalene on July 22, with the Gloria at Mass and her encounter with the risen Jesus read as the Gospel.

original.note: Greek: apostle, one who is sent, from apostellō, to send.

trapdoor: what you thought: Mary Magdalene was a minor follower.
what it means: she's the first in John sent to announce the resurrection, to the apostles themselves.
what a scholar hears: 'apostle of the apostles' appears in medieval writers (e.g. Rabanus Maurus, Thomas Aquinas); the 2016 decree of the Congregation for Divine Worship used the title.

sources.quoted: Jesus saith to her: Mary. She turning, saith to him: Rabboni (which is to say, Master).

sources.ref: Decree on the celebration of St. Mary Magdalene (2016)

notes: 'Woman, why weepest thou?' and her answer are given without quotation marks; close to Douay wording.
Feast of St. Mary Magdalene: decree dated June 3, 2016, at Pope Francis's wish; the decree and an accompanying article by Archbishop Roche used 'apostolorum apostola'. Confirm.
'Very early, Christian writers gave her a title': often traced to Hippolytus (who calls the women 'apostles to the apostles') and later to Rabanus Maurus and Aquinas. Confirm wording.
Mē mou haptou as 'don't cling / hold on to me': widely accepted reading of the present imperative. Confirm.
